implementation_notes: Ruby's core gives threads and thread-safe queues but no executor and no Future: Thread::Queue (or SizedQueue for a bound) is the activation queue and Thread.new { ... } running a pop loop is the scheduler, while the caller receives a per-request reply queue or waits on a Mutex/ConditionVariable for the result - the manually built stand-in for the pattern's Future. The servant runs only in the worker thread, so it needs no locking. MRI's GVL means real parallelism only for blocking I/O or C extensions, so use this for decoupling and ordering, and move heavy work to a background job system or a Ractor.
pitfalls: Queue#pop blocks forever when nothing arrives: without an explicit stop message (and a worker join) the thread outlives the test run or the process hangs at exit.
Thread::Queue is unbounded; SizedQueue gives back-pressure by blocking producers.
An exception in the worker thread kills the scheduler silently (report_on_exception prints, the object still looks alive); rescue inside the loop and complete the reply exceptionally.
